correctness.rationale: Fix d≥2, and split the quotient directions into span(1) and its perpendicular; the coupling eigenvalues are d+1 and 1. On the diagonal α=(d+1)h, and each x_σ solves α sin x_σ=π, giving the two distinct antipodal prime-two orbits. At the representative x_σ set t=α cos x_σ. The recentered two-step return has derivative 1−t²=−1−ε and chain-rule second and third derivatives π(3t+t²) and 4t²+3t³+t⁴−3π²(1+t). Thus as t²=2 the flip coefficient g''²/4+g'''/6 is (2+t)(5π²+2)/2>0. Dividing the two-step return's second iterate minus the identity by the offset y gives a smooth function with strict local concavity, maximum 2ε+O(ε²) at y=O(ε), and negative values at fixed close endpoints. There are exactly two nonparent roots for ε>0 and none for ε<0; the return exchanges them because its only nearby fixed point is the parent. They have offsets ±sqrt(ε/B_σ)+O(ε); differentiating yields longitudinal four-step multiplier 1−4ε+O(ε^(3/2)). The leading ratio sqrt(B_−/B_+)=sqrt(2)−1, and oddness exchanges the two cycles (mapping a representative neighborhood to the other cycle's antipodal neighborhood). At the parent the transverse four-step derivative is q_d I with q_d=(1−2/(d+1)²)²∈(0,1). The projected four-step fixed-point equation has invertible perpendicular derivative (q_d−1)I, so its unique local transverse solution is the invariant diagonal. This excludes all nondiagonal local daughters on both sides. All transverse multipliers along each daughter equal q_d+O_d(sqrt(ε)), proving attraction in the full quotient for each fixed d. Neither global attraction nor stability in an unquotiented common-rotation direction is asserted. Independent finite brackets for ε=10⁻⁴ and 4·10⁻⁴ supported the offsets and multipliers; the uploaded code was read, not run, and the existence, count and stability follow from the local analysis rather than the brackets.
